chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from al-Hasan ibn Hudhayfa from Jamil from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The slave does not inherit and the free person does not inherit.

key_terms.الطَّلِيقُ: The free person (one who is not a slave)

ai.seo_question: Does a slave inherit from a free person in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'hijab al-'asl' (blocking by origin), where the fundamental difference in status between a slave and a free person prevents mutual inheritance. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is derived from the Quranic verse 4:11 and is understood to apply specifically to the slave owned by the deceased, emphasizing that the legal barrier of 'difference in status' (ikhtilaf al-'asl) supersedes other kinship ties in this specific context.
